note: The four-state half of hif-backend#61, and the corpus's first Verilog tri-state - the existing bidirectional designs, vhdl_tristate_pad and vhdl_shared_bus, are all VHDL-sourced. `{4{1'bz}}` has to keep its operand widths, which no reparse can check because verilog2hif accepts an unsized concatenation operand, and it has to stay high-impedance rather than becoming an ordinary logic level. The testbench is the second device on the pin, so releasing and driving are distinguishable; without one, a pad that never let go would produce the same trace. The pin is driven and never read back: a process reading the resolved value of an inout it also drives is a separate path, and one hif2verilog gets wrong today.
